title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for type 2 diabetes.

History of Present Illness
The patient is a known case of type 2 diabetes mellitus presenting today for routine management. He reports adherence to his current regimen. He denies any acute changes in symptoms and states he has had no complications to report since the last visit. He continues to manage his type 2 diabetes with insulin therapy.

Medication List
Insulin (long-term use)

Examination
Vitals are stable. Physical examination is unremarkable, and the patient shows no signs of acute distress or complications.

Assessment
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, with no complications noted at this time. The patient remains stable on long-term insulin therapy.

Plan
Continue current regimen of insulin. Follow up in three months for routine check and supply check. Encourage consistent monitoring of blood glucose levels.
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
